finding.name: Stack-based Buffer Overflow
finding.summary: scanf("%s", code) has no field width, so an input token longer than 15 characters overflows the 16-byte code stack array.

trap: Adding a field width of scanf("%16s", code) looks like it matches the 16-byte array but still overflows by one: an %Ns conversion reads up to N characters and then appends a terminating NUL, so %16s can write 17 bytes into a 16-byte array. The field width must be one less than the destination's size - %15s for char code[16] - to leave room for the NUL.
must_preserve: read_ticket_code still reads a whitespace-delimited token from stdin into code and, when it fits, copies it into out (bounded by out_capacity) and returns 0. An input token that does not fit in code is rejected (returns -1) rather than silently truncated.
